name: Domaine Paul Autard Châteauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée La Cote Ronde 2015
text:
## Domaine Paul Autard Châteauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée La Côte Ronde 2015

**The story.** Domaine Paul Autard is based in [Courthézon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Paul+Autard,+Courth%C3%A9zon,+France&t=k), on the eastern edge of the [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC) appellation, where the Autard family has farmed for several generations. Jean-Paul Autard took charge while still a teenager and built its reputation for wines of density and precision; a new cellar was completed in 2005, and his children Pauline and Jules now work alongside him ([Rue Pinard](https://ruepinard.com/en/wine/producer.domaine-paul-autard)). The family has about 26 hectares, half of them in Châteauneuf, with vines averaging over 50 years old (40 to 96 years), farmed with *culture raisonnée*, a "reasoned" approach that limits chemical treatments. The style is modern: destemmed grapes, mechanical punch-downs, and ageing in small oak barrels from new to three years old ([Sommelier Academy](https://sommelier-academy.de/topic/court-of-master-sommeliers-notable-producers-paul-autard/)).

**The wine: La Côte Ronde.** La Côte Ronde, first made in 1989, is an unusual Châteauneuf: half [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), half [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), from 90-year-old vines in the Le Mourre de Gaud lieu-dit, aged 18 months in small new oak barrels ([Sommelier Academy](https://sommelier-academy.de/topic/court-of-master-sommeliers-notable-producers-paul-autard/)). Jeff Leve calls it "one of the most modern styled wines in Chateauneuf du Pape today" ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/2017/08/2015-chateauneuf-du-pape-tasting-notes-harvest-report-top-250-wines/)). With that much Syrah and new oak, it is darker, spicier and more oak-framed than a traditional Grenache-led Châteauneuf.

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) says Grenache suffered from [coulure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulure) at flowering in 2015 (many flowers failed to set into grapes), so yields were lower but quality very promising, with alcohol higher than in the two previous years. She doesn't expect the 2015s to live as long as the 2016s. [John Livingstone-Learmonth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Livingstone-Learmonth), writing for [Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/learn/vintage-guides/rhone-vintage-guides/chateauneuf-du-pape-2015-gigondas-vacqueyras-366743/), called it a generally very good year with robust reds and fine tannins, though some Châteauneuf came out a little "hot". A 50% Syrah blend was well placed in a year short of Grenache.

**What the critics say for 2015.**
- **Jeff Leve, [The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/2017/08/2015-chateauneuf-du-pape-tasting-notes-harvest-report-top-250-wines/): 92** (2017). Smoke, espresso and vanilla first, then deep red fruit; "fat, round and forward, with density of fruit and flavor, along with a lot of oak".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.7** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (Wine Spectator also reviewed it, but I couldn't read the note, so I've left the score out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2018 to 2031. With a decade in bottle, the new oak should have melted into the fruit, leaving dark cherry, espresso, spice and smoke. It is in its prime; decant an hour ahead.

**Serving and food.** Serve at 16 to 17°C. The oak and Syrah suit barbecue: grilled rib eye, smoked brisket, lamb with a spice crust, or duck breast with cherries.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Paul Autard at the moment.

**From the history books**
- **Five communes.** Châteauneuf's vineyards lie around Châteauneuf-du-Pape itself and in neighbouring [Bédarrides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9darrides), [Courthézon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courth%C3%A9zon) and [Sorgues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorgues), between Avignon and Orange ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **The popes.** "Châteauneuf-du-Pape" means "the Pope's new castle": in 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to Avignon ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **Bigger than the north.** Châteauneuf makes over 110,000 hectolitres a year, more than the whole northern Rhône ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
